name: Release Management Checklist
description: This module is a pre-completion checklist for release management work: a short set of checks to run before calling a release management task done.
content:
This module is a pre-completion checklist for release management work: a short set of checks to run before calling a release management task done.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Keep release management changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
2. When multiple release management strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
3. Prefer the simplest release management approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
4. Check that release management terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
5. Validate release management outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
6. State assumptions about release management explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
7. Re-check edge cases relevant to release management (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
8. Keep release management outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not apply generic release management advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Do not silently drop release management edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Do not skip documenting release management assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of release management correctness.
- Avoid introducing new release management abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for release management, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
